newsitem.title: USA: Florida town drops youth ban on tobacco products.
newsitem.headline: Florida town drops youth ban on tobacco products.

text.p: An eastern Florida resort community decided on Wednesday it would not become the first city in the state to outlaw possession of tobacco products by minors.
By a 3-2 vote, city commissioners on Wednesday night rejected an ordinance that would have levied fines or community service on minors for possessing any kind of tobacco products.

Florida law prohibits the sale of tobacco products to minors, but does not stop them from smoking cigarettes or chewing tobacco if they already have the products. Backers of the ban argued that this sent the wrong message to kids, telling them they were not responsible for their own health.
The Ormond Beach ordinance would have outlawed possession and punished offenders with fines up to $25 or 50 hours of community service.
Commissioner Carl Persis, who sponsored the ordinance, based on a similar law in Englewood, Colo., said he had received hundreds of telephone calls and letters from supporters.
"Parents need some help. We all know that nicotine is addictive. Eighty to 90 percent of adult smokers started before they were 18," Persis said.
But Mayor Dave Hood saw the issue differently.

"If this child is fined, and simply chooses not to pay this fine, then what is our remedy? Only incarceration," Hood said. He had support from both the American Lung Association and the American Cancer Society, whose officials sent letters saying their organisations would oppose laws which could result in children being arrested. The American Civil Liberties Union also said it opposed the ban.
